paragraphs: Grave Discover Software sells a web-based cemetery management system that cemetery managers use to maintain burial information and grave locations. The same system lets a cemetery grant the public access to that data along with a searchable map.

Records are digitized into an inventory of burials, occupants, plot owners, deeds, grave types, grave locations and headstone images. The information sits on cloud-based servers that the company says are backed up daily. That is offered in contrast to desktop software, where backups depend on the cemetery's own computer environment. The interactive map can be viewed in four different ways. Public users can search grave occupant information by name, date of birth, date of burial, date of death and type of veteran. A visitor standing in the cemetery can pull the software up on a mobile device through a custom cemetery URL to find the grave they are seeking.

Cemeteries shown on the site include Mica Hill Cemetery, which is located in Durham, CT and operated by Durham Cemetery Company. A cemetery board uses the software to manage one cemetery along with other small cemeteries in its care. The company describes a team made up of designers, developers and usability specialists. It says it aims for software that is user-friendly and affordable.

quote.text: Cemeteries contain decades and sometimes centuries of historical information documenting beloved people; maintaining accurate records is essential.
